name: Caséta Smart Dimmer PD-6WCL (US)

radios.note: The dimmer talks to the bridge on Lutron's own 431-437 MHz radio (Clear Connect), which our radio list lacks. Ethernet is the bridge's link to your router; the dimmer has no Wi-Fi.

matter.note: No Matter claim found on the Lutron pages we saw; not confirmed either way.

apple_home.note: Lutron says the Smart Bridge carries Apple HomeKit technology, so the dimmer shows up in Apple Home through the bridge.

google_home.note: Lutron lists Google Assistant and Google Home; it reaches the dimmer through the Smart Bridge.

alexa.note: Lutron lists Alexa voice control; it needs the Smart Bridge.

smartthings.note: Lutron's integrations page lists SmartThings; it works through the Smart Bridge. The page looked dated, so check it is still current.

home_assistant.note: Home Assistant's Lutron Caséta integration connects to the Smart Bridge over the local network (local push).

hubRequired.note: Lutron says remote access, scenes, schedules and voice assistants need the Smart Bridge (now called Smart Hub). Without it the dimmer pairs only with Pico remotes and sensors.

localControl.note: Home Assistant talks to the bridge locally. The bridge keeps running schedules and Pico remotes working if the internet drops, per Lutron.

switchForm.note: Replaces a standard single-pole wall dimmer in a 1-gang US wallbox.

dimmer.note: Rated 150 W for LED and 600 W for incandescent or halogen, with a 25 W minimum.

neutralRequired.note: Two-wire design that installs like a regular switch. A ground wire is optional unless local code demands it.

gangs.note: Lutron's spec calls for a 1-gang US wallbox.

summary: Lutron's Caséta PD-6WCL is a two-wire wall dimmer that replaces a standard US switch and needs no neutral. On its own it pairs only with Pico remotes and Lutron sensors; app control, schedules and voice control all go through the Caséta Smart Bridge. With the bridge, Lutron lists Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa and SmartThings, and Home Assistant has a local integration for it. It handles 150 W of LED or 600 W of incandescent.
caveats: Needs the Caséta Smart Bridge (now called Smart Hub) for app, voice and ecosystem control; the bridge plugs into your router by Ethernet.
LED loads are limited to 150 W, with a 25 W minimum, and the bulbs must be dimmable.
Home Assistant does not receive button presses from the wired dimmer, only from Pico remotes.
